task.title: Make quota pauses probeable and self-recovering

scope.owned_layer: Provider failure classification, dispatch-pause recovery gates, bounded targeted recovery probing, and supervisor regression evidence.
scope.not_changing: Provider credentials, account/quota grouping, configured probe values, runtime-state JSON, reviewer policy, service processes, rollout, and product code.

contract.probe_classification: quota_reached is quota_terminal/degraded even when the failure text also contains authentication-probe wording; only credential statuses classify as auth/revoked.
contract.pause_expiry: An expired quota or capacity pause becomes a live-recovery-probe gate and continues blocking dispatch instead of disappearing on wall-clock expiry.
contract.recovery_authority: Only an authoritative probe with source=live and a checked_at at or after the gate boundary may clear a probe-gated pause; cached success is insufficient.
contract.bounded_probing: Due recovery probes are de-duplicated by provider dispatch group, capped per cycle, and failed probes schedule next_recovery_probe_at from the failed-probe interval.
contract.refresh_independence: Targeted recovery probing consumes the pre-lock runtime snapshot and still runs when supervisor.auto_refresh_provider_capabilities is false.
contract.auth_semantics: Authentication pauses remain sticky until a fresh live success; a recovery probe that reveals auth upgrades the existing pause to the sticky auth gate.
contract.lock_boundary: Recovery probe subprocesses run in probe_provider_reports before _run_once_locked acquires runtime admission; the locked phase only reconciles probe results.
